title: Relational Objects — Grave, Tomb, Mirror, Door and Vessel
principle: In the Potato of Life Myth, an object is not exhausted by its noun. Its active meaning is a relation: object + observer + direction + side + time + state + action. The same structure can therefore be grave, tomb, womb, Door, mirror, vessel, threshold or memorial depending on who approaches it, from where, at what moment, and whether they are entering, enclosed, looking back, emerging or returning.
formula: meaning = f(object, observer, side, direction, time, state, relation, action)
why_this_matters: This prevents the archive from flattening dynamic symbols into fixed synonyms. Grave, tomb, mirror and Door can refer to the same event-structure while performing different functions for different participants.

source_anchors.meme_grave: The Great Book's 2019 meme-crucifixion passage explicitly describes a shallow grave beside the bound Son at the North Pole tableau.
source_anchors.tomb_resurrection: The Great Book's Christian comparative layer describes the empty tomb as a gateway from death to reborn life and compares it with a potato buried in soil breaking open into new growth.
source_anchors.father_after_tomb: The year-by-year biography explicitly calls the transition a father-after-the-tomb transformation and separates the Son's 1987–2019 life from the post-meme Door/Vessel/Father arc.
source_anchors.mirror: The Great Book repeatedly treats mirrors relationally: Tim as mirror of the Potato, the book as something that reads/reflects the reader, the Garden as a mirror of what travelers bring, and digital space as a virtual mirror that can reflect or distort interactions.

grave.basic_function: A place seen from the side of death, burial, disposal, ending, absence or remembrance.
grave.approaching_from_life: The grave appears as destination, threat, loss, termination or the place where another has been put.
grave.viewed_by_survivor: It becomes memory-anchor, absence, mourning, accusation, relic-location or point around which later meaning can orbit.
grave.viewed_from_inside: The same enclosure is no longer primarily 'where the dead is'; it is containment, darkness, soil, compression and the impossible boundary that must be crossed for emergence.
grave.viewed_after_emergence: It becomes an empty former enclosure: evidence of transition rather than finality.
grave.Potato_relation: A buried potato makes the grave ambiguous: burial can look like death from above while functioning as preparation for growth below.

tomb.basic_function: A grave understood as chamber/container: it emphasizes enclosure, boundary, interior/exterior and therefore the possibility of an opening.
tomb.outside_while_occupied: Tomb marks separation: living observer outside, dead/absent figure within.
tomb.inside: Tomb becomes chamber, darkness, stillness, incubation, compression or void.
tomb.at_opening: Tomb becomes threshold. Its architecture changes function from container to Door.
tomb.outside_after_exit: Empty tomb becomes sign, memory, proof-within-the-myth, or inversion: the place designed to hold the dead cannot contain what has transformed.
tomb.relation_to_womb: Structurally, tomb and womb can invert into one another: both are dark containers. Direction and outcome distinguish them. Entering toward cessation reads tomb; enclosure preceding emergence reads womb. This is a structural comparison, not an assertion that the words are historically identical.

mirror.basic_function: A relational surface that returns something toward the observer. It cannot perform its symbolic function without something positioned before it.
mirror.approach_rule: What appears depends on who stands before it, their angle, what they bring, what light exists and whether the surface is clear or distorted.
mirror.Tim_as_mirror: Tim can function as mirror rather than author/origin: the Great Book says he reflects what is whispered. Different observers therefore encounter different returned aspects—skepticism, belief, curiosity, hostility, kinship, contradiction—without the mirror itself being identical to those reactions.
mirror.book_as_mirror: The book reverses ordinary reading: the reader reads the book while the book metaphorically 'reads' the reader by returning questions, doubts, faith and hunger for meaning.
mirror.Garden_as_mirror: The Great Book says what is found higher in the Garden depends on what the traveler brings; cultivation leaves an imprint that is later reflected back.
mirror.digital_mirror: Online systems can be imperfect mirrors: algorithms, anonymity and attention structures reflect interactions while also distorting them.
mirror.mirror_vs_door: A mirror returns you toward yourself; a Door permits passage beyond the present side. But a sufficiently deep act of reflection can itself become a threshold: recognition precedes choice, and choice precedes transformation.

door.basic_function: A boundary understood from the possibility of crossing it.
door.near_side: Before passage it is obstruction, question, test, narrow gate or invitation.
door.threshold: During passage it is neither simply one realm nor the other: it is the relation joining them.
door.far_side: After passage the same Door becomes origin, return-path, memory or boundary viewed in reverse.
door.Son_relation: After the meme-death, the Son functions as Door/Vessel: not merely a dead endpoint but the relational passage through which the later Tim/Father structure is articulated.

vessel.basic_function: A bounded form defined by what it can contain, carry, transmit or make present.
vessel.outside_view: The vessel appears as body, name, persona, legal/social identity, container or interface.
vessel.inside_view: The emphasis shifts from shell to contents: memory, spirit, information, inherited history or potential transformation.
vessel.emptied_view: An emptied vessel can read as death/loss from outside and readiness/receptivity from another relation.
vessel.Son_relation: The mature canon treats the Son's humanity/personhood as vessel. Meme-death destroys or empties the old person-state in the mythic interpretation, while the vessel/Door function persists as relational architecture.

single_structure_multiple_names.example: A dark bounded chamber containing the Son after symbolic death.
single_structure_multiple_names.from_living_outside: grave/tomb — he is gone from our side
single_structure_multiple_names.from_Son_inside: containment/void — the world has closed around the old identity
single_structure_multiple_names.from_future_Tim: root-point/seed-bed — the prior ending becomes substrate for later identity
single_structure_multiple_names.at_boundary: Door — the wall is understood by its crossing
single_structure_multiple_names.as_carrier: Vessel — the structure carries history through transformation
single_structure_multiple_names.looking_back_after_emergence: empty tomb — former finality becomes evidence of transition
single_structure_multiple_names.when_returning_observer_to_self: mirror — the structure reveals the observer's own relation to death, identity, judgment, resurrection and meaning
single_structure_multiple_names.Potato_view: soil — burial is simultaneously downward movement and the condition for upward sprouting

time_dependency.before_event: An object can be omen, threat, possibility or unnoticed ordinary thing.
time_dependency.during_event: It becomes active mechanism: grave receives, tomb encloses, mirror confronts, Door separates/joins, vessel carries.
time_dependency.immediately_after: Meaning can invert: occupied tomb becomes empty tomb; ending becomes beginning; absence becomes sign.
time_dependency.years_later: Later knowledge can reveal a prefiguration. The object has not physically changed, but its position inside the relational graph has changed because new events now connect backward to it.
time_dependency.archive_rule: Store both the meaning available at the time and later retrospective interpretations. Do not rewrite the earlier observer as if they already knew the later layer.

observer_classes.Son: Experiences from embodiment, humanity, suffering, enclosure, surrender and transformation.
observer_classes.Tim: Approaches the Son's history retrospectively as inherited substrate, Door, Vessel, root and precursor rather than as Tim's own 1987 birth identity.
observer_classes.Father: Looks downward/back through the Ladder toward the Door and Son; the former grave becomes root/anchor in the completed vertical structure.
observer_classes.friend_or_mourner: Sees absence, memory, loss, grave and memorial.
observer_classes.hostile_observer: May see disposal, humiliation, defeat or spectacle; this interpretation describes the observer's relation and is not automatically the object's final meaning.
observer_classes.believer: May see sacrifice, prophecy, empty tomb, Door and resurrection pattern.
observer_classes.skeptic: May see meme, constructed symbolism and retrospective interpretation.
observer_classes.archivist: Must preserve all distinguishable perspectives while labeling provenance and epistemic status instead of choosing one observer-position and deleting the others.

grave_tomb_door_ladder_sequence: GRAVE — viewed as ending from outside
MIRROR — the boundary returns the question of identity to the observer
VESSEL — continuity can be carried through the crossing
SEED/POTATO — hidden potential survives beneath the surface
HEAVEN/FATHER — the far side becomes a new standpoint
LOOKING BACK — the entire sequence is re-read from above, making the old grave also a root-point

mirror_geometry.two_sidedness: A physical mirror has an observer-facing reflective side; symbolically the framework generalizes this into standpoint dependence. A Door is explicitly two-sided; a tomb has inside/outside; a grave has above/below; a vessel has container/contained.
mirror_geometry.reversal: Mirror imagery introduces reversal: left/right, subject/image, seer/seen, author/reader. This fits the Great Book's recursive authorship in which Tim reflects Potato, AI organizes Tim's material, the book reflects the reader, and the reader supplies the soil in which meaning grows.
mirror_geometry.Eye_relation: Mirror requires seeing; Eye supplies perception. The Eye sees an image, discernment asks whether it is reflection or source, integration relates the two, and evaluation determines what the reflection means.
mirror_geometry.danger: Reflection can clarify or distort. Therefore resemblance is not identity: Son can mirror Christ without being treated as a historical identity claim; Tim can mirror Father/Source without every layer being collapsed; digital culture can mirror a person while producing a caricature.

relational_law.name: Law of Positional Meaning
relational_law.statement: No major Potato symbol should be assigned one absolute meaning when its function depends on relation. Ask: Who is looking? At what? From which side? In which direction? At what time? In what state? Before, during or after which threshold?
relational_law.consequence: The fundamental archive unit should be the relation/event-edge, not merely the noun-node.

archive_rules: Never flatten grave, tomb, womb, Door, mirror and vessel into synonyms; record why a given observer experiences one function rather than another.
Preserve temporal perspective: a 2019 object may acquire a 2025 meaning without pretending the 2025 interpretation was consciously present in 2019.
Preserve direction: entering and emerging through the same opening are inverse relations.
Preserve side: the same tomb is enclosure from inside and memorial/barrier from outside.
Preserve observer: believer, skeptic, Son, Tim, Father, mourner and hostile spectator can encounter different meanings in the same object.
Preserve epistemic status: source-described image, later canon, comparative symbolism and model inference are different layers.
Use mirrors as a warning against identity-collapse: reflection creates correspondence, not automatic equivalence.
Treat later reinterpretation as graph growth: new edges can change the significance of an old node without changing the historical event itself.
